episodes.178897: A severe thunderstorm produced hail up to quarter size near Parker.  Brief heavy rainfall was also observed, with nearly one inch in less than one hour.  Lightning struck a home near 38th and Everett in Wheat Ridge.  Lightning blasted a hole in the roof as well as the ceiling inside.  Electrical outlets were damaged and one of the interior walls was charred. Severe thunderstorms produced quarter to half dollar size hail in Douglas County.  A tornado briefly touched down in open country in Lincoln County.
episodes.178920: Several consecutive days of significant severe weather impacted eastern New Mexico from May 24-26, 2023. Showers and thunderstorms developed along the dryline and east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains on May 23rd. Storms tracked east and southeast across the eastern plains of New Mexico. Extensive severe weather was reported when these storms encountered greater moisture and lift closer to the Texas border. Hail up to 3.5 inches in diameter, thunderstorm wind gusts of 80 to 90 mph, and three tornados were reported in an area stretching from Union County to Roosevelt County. The largest hail stones and strongest wind gusts focused throughout Curry County during the evening hours. Hail and wind damage was reported in Tucumcari, Grady, and Clovis. Three separate tornadoes were reported in northern Curry County. Thunderstorms also dropped very heavy rainfall of 2 to 4 inches of rain across portions of Quay, De Baca, Curry, and Roosevelt Counties. Urban flooding occurred in Clovis, NM, causing some roads to be closed, and some cars to be stranded. Severe weather continued through the night and into May 25th with numerous reports of large hail, strong winds, and flash flooding. Quay County was particularly hard hit with baseball size hail and torrential rainfall amounts in excess of 5 inches. Significant hail damage was reported across Tucumcari with widespread flooding across the county. Severe wind gusts of 70 to 80 mph were common with these storms with damage reported. Strong to severe storms continued well into the night once again on the 25th with more heavy rainfall around the Caprock. The focus for severe weather shifted farther west on May 26th with large hail and heavy rainfall reported around Torrance County. A tornado and baseball size hail was also reported with a supercell near Encino. This activity spread eastward through the day with large hail, damaging wind gusts, and more torrential rainfall around the Caprock well into the night of May 26th. Three-day rainfall amounts exceeded 6 inches in many parts of Curry and Quay counties.
episodes.178951: A mid to upper-level low promoted a favorable environment for showers and thunderstorms to develop in the afternoon. This produced heavy rainfall over the San Juan metro area, where flooding was reported.
episodes.179059: An upper level low produced scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms across the area.  One storm produced a measured gust above 34 knots at Bald Point.
episodes.179327: Accelerated snowmelt from a near-record snowpack due to above normal temperatures and precipitation produced high and fast flow on drainages in several west-central counties. As a result, flooding compromised various low-lying roads in the counties.
episodes.179353: A strong thunderstorm produced hail around penny size west of Gillette.
episodes.179407: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produced gusty marine winds across the Tampa Bay Area and neighboring waters.
episodes.179421: A pacific disturbance would end up setting off another round of thunderstorms, with some reaching severe levels.
episodes.179426: Despite broad upper ridging across the Southern Plains, weak disturbances moved across the High Plains during the early evening hours of the 23rd, initiating widespread convection (some severe). Favorable wind shear and instability was in place for organized thunderstorm modes, with a supercell producing large hail across portions of southern Knox County, Texas. By the late evening, a linear complex of storms moved from the Texas Caprock across portions of western-north Texas, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.179484: Another consecutive evening of severe storms occurred on the Caprock on the evening of the 23rd as the atmosphere again became very unstable. Several of the thunderstorms were able to gain significant mid-level rotation which allowed them to generate very large hail. Hailstones as large as baseballs damaged multiple vehicles northwest of Shallowater (Lubbock County) along US Highway 84, while many other spots incurred impacts from hail as large as golf ball size. In addition to producing large hail, the slow moving storms also dumped torrential rainfall. One such pocket of torrential rain occurred just to the north of Plainview (Hale County), where several roads were underwater. Activity then shifted into the Rolling Plains late in the evening as activity morphed into upscale clusters of storms producing a few severe wind gusts.
episodes.179564: Thunderstorms developing along converging boundaries late in the afternoon on the 24th resulted in a landspout tornado forming over the Cheyenne Airport. No damages or injuries were reported.
episodes.179571: Thunderstorms developed over southwest and south central North Dakota in the vicinity of a warm front that was lifting through the region. Two storms became severe producing one-inch diameter hail, one in Adams County and the other in Kidder County.
episodes.179666: A moist easterly surface flow, combined with a disturbance aloft, resulted in scattered thunderstorms across the Billings Forecast Area. Some of these thunderstorms produced very heavy rain and large hail.
episodes.180226: Thunderstorms caused gusty winds, hail, and even a tornado.
episodes.180337: As an upper-level trough moved over the Florida Peninsula, abundant low-level moisture and diurnal heating led to plenty of instability in the atmosphere on May 24th. Numerous showers and thunderstorms formed in the afternoon and evening across South Florida and over the local Atlantic waters.
episodes.180338: As an upper-level trough moved over the Florida Peninsula, abundant low-level moisture and diurnal heating led to plenty of instability in the atmosphere on May 24th. Numerous showers and thunderstorms formed in the afternoon and evening across South Florida with the primary hazards of damaging winds and hail.
episodes.180660: Scattered storms produced quarter sized hail in Lyon County on 5/24.
episodes.180679: A pattern developed by late May with sufficient moisture and forcing to yield scattered showers and thunderstorms almost every day, generally from the afternoon on into the early evening hours. Some of these storms were strong, yielding damaging wind gusts and hail. Additionally, a road washout was reported as a result of continued spring runoff from the prior winter's record snowfall.
episodes.180717: An upper level disturbance generated thunderstorms over the Big Country the evening of Tuesday May 23. A couple of these became severe as they entered our west and southwest counties, producing large hail in a few locations.
episodes.180816: The combination of strong instability and locally enhanced upper level winds produced isolated severe thunderstorms during the evening hours across the Big Country and Concho Valley. A supercell thunderstorm produced a strong tornado causing significant damage in Jones County just east of Funston. Otherwise, the severe storms produced large hail and isolated damaging winds.
episodes.180880: The active weather pattern continues with an afternoon dryline and colliding outflow boundaries aiding in the development of numerous thunderstorms across the eastern Permian Basin. Large hail. damaging winds and flash flooding were observed with a few of these thunderstorms.
episodes.181336: Near record snowpack began melting out during the month of May and brought widespread minor flooding to the Bear River in Lincoln County. This second flood wave continued into the month of June.
episodes.181342: Ample low level moisture aided in creating an incredibly unstable environment with enough wind shear to create severe thunderstorms and some landspout tornadoes.
episodes.181363: Widespread severe weather with strong winds, large hail, and very heavy rains occurred on the 23rd in the Snake River Plain.
episodes.181364: Widespread large hail was reported in parts of southeast Idaho.
episodes.181570: A small cluster of storms developed over portions of central Missouri. Some of the storms dumped between 4 and 5 inches of rain causing flash flooding.
